title: The four fixed waits off the normal workers end on events: the io_uring ring thread, the generic-IO bridge, run_until_exit and the standard-IO server
purpose: B-181's wake-edge enumeration (EMBEDDER-COMPOSITION-SPEC §3.8.1, beamr main 001be4ad) found four waits of a set length outside the normal workers, which B-181 does not cover. Waffles ruled on Cambium on 21 October 2026 at 04:49 (Melbourne), post c38bfbeb, that they are Tom's no-fixed-waits rule found in the code and get a brief id and a date today; Hermes agreed (04:50, post 1440ba67) and reviews this brief. Read at beamr main 001be4ad: (1) the Linux io_uring ring thread loops on op_receiver.recv_timeout(RING_TICK), RING_TICK 10 ms (crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:23, :222), so with operations in flight a completion waits up to 10 ms to be drained and an idle ring wakes 100 times a second; (2) the generic-IO bridge's completion thread loops on ring.poll_completions(Duration::from_millis(100)) while a shutdown flag is unset (io/bridge.rs:92-97), so it wakes ten times a second for nothing and a shutdown waits up to 100 ms; (3) Scheduler::run_until_exit loops on wake_condvar.wait_timeout(10 ms) until the pid's exit tombstone appears (scheduler/execution.rs:188-203), and nothing notifies it on a process exit, so every host waiter polls; (4) the standard-IO server's wait_for_completion loops on ring.poll_completions(POLL_TIMEOUT), 10 ms (io/standard_io.rs:19, :216-224), reached from handle_message through run_available, which the enumeration found has no caller (W16). The CompletionRing trait offers only poll_completions(timeout) (io/ring.rs:150-156), so every consumer of a ring has to choose a timeout; the thread pool's own answer is a channel recv_timeout (io/thread_pool.rs:168-179). This brief gives each wait the event it is waiting for, and removes the standard-IO path if nothing reaches it.
task: Give CompletionRing a blocking wait that returns on a completion or on the ring's shutdown, in crates/beamr/src/io/ring.rs, with its implementations in io/thread_pool.rs, io/uring.rs and the failed and replay rings; move the bridge (io/bridge.rs) and, if it is live, the standard-IO server (io/standard_io.rs) onto it; make the io_uring ring thread block in the kernel until a completion or a new submission (io/uring.rs); and give a process exit the B-181 wake edge so run_until_exit waits without a timeout (scheduler/execution.rs). Tests go in crates/beamr/src/io/blocking_waits_tests.rs (new) and beside the scheduler's exit tests.

requirements.title: A ring consumer waits for a completion or the ring's shutdown, never for a set time
requirements.spec: Behavioural. THE SYSTEM SHALL add to CompletionRing (crates/beamr/src/io/ring.rs:150) a wait_completions(&self) -> RingWait that blocks until at least one completion is available, answering RingWait::Completions(Vec<IoCompletion>) with every completion then available, or until the ring is shut down, answering RingWait::Shutdown, and SHALL implement it for every ring: the thread pool by a blocking receive on its completion channel that a shutdown disconnects or wakes (io/thread_pool.rs:168-179), io_uring through its completion channel likewise, and the failed and replay rings from their own queues. The generic-IO bridge's completion thread (io/bridge.rs:92-97) SHALL loop on wait_completions and end on Shutdown, with its shutdown flag kept only if a test shows it is still needed; poll_completions SHALL stay for callers that pass a timeout of zero or need one, and every remaining caller of poll_completions with a non-zero timeout SHALL be named in the handback with its reason or moved.
acceptance: Red first (nextest, beamr, src/io/blocking_waits_tests.rs): a bridge over a thread-pool ring with nothing in flight makes no wake of its completion thread over a span the test bounds by events (a submission and its completion, then a second), counted by a seam on the thread's loop; today it wakes every 100 ms.

Red: a submitted file read's completion is dispatched by the bridge with no timeout elapsed in between, ending on the completion's dispatch; shutting the ring down ends the bridge thread, joined by the test, with no timeout in the loop.
Red: wait_completions on each ring type answers Shutdown after the ring's shutdown, and Completions with every available completion otherwise.

requirements.title: The io_uring ring thread blocks in the kernel until a completion or a new submission
requirements.spec: Behavioural. THE SYSTEM SHALL replace the ring thread's recv_timeout(RING_TICK) loop (crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:205-230) with a wait that ends on an event: with nothing in flight, a blocking receive of the next RingMessage; with operations in flight, a kernel wait for at least one completion (submit_and_wait(1)) that a new submission or a shutdown also ends, by an eventfd the submit side writes and the ring holds a read on, so a submission made while the thread waits in the kernel is picked up at once and not after a tick. RING_TICK SHALL be removed. The ring's ordering, its drain_cqes and its shutdown (in_flight empty and the flag set) SHALL behave as today.
acceptance: Red (the same file, cfg(target_os = "linux")): with one read in flight, a second submitted while the ring thread waits in the kernel completes without the first completing first, ending on the second's completion; today the second waits for the next 10 ms tick.
Red: an idle io_uring ring's thread makes no loop iteration between two submissions the test makes, counted by a seam.
The Linux tests run on a Linux venue Waffles names; until one exists the handback states R2 as NOT CONFIRMED by a run, with the reason, and never as passed.

requirements.title: A host waiting for a process's exit is woken by the exit
requirements.spec: Behavioural. THE SYSTEM SHALL give a process exit the wake edge of B-181 (take the wait_set lock, advance the wake sequence, notify_all) once the exit tombstone and result are recorded (scheduler/execution.rs:150-180), and Scheduler::run_until_exit (:188-203) SHALL read the sequence, check the tombstone, and wait on wake_condvar with no timeout while, under the wait_set lock, the sequence is unchanged, so an exit between its check and its wait is never lost. The same SHALL hold for every other host-side wait in the scheduler that today waits with a set timeout for a process's state, each named in the handback by file and line.
acceptance: Red (nextest, beamr, beside the scheduler's exit tests): run_until_exit on a process that exits on a message the test sends returns its exit reason with no timeout in the wait, ending on the return; today the loop wakes every 10 ms, counted by a seam on its loop, and after the change it wakes once, on the exit.

Red: 1,000 run_until_exit calls racing their processes' exits from another thread all return, each ending on its return, with the wait unbounded; a lost exit would hang, and nextest's slow-timeout reports it.

requirements.title: The standard-IO server's poll is removed if nothing reaches it, and blocks on an event if something does
requirements.spec: Behavioural. The build SHALL first establish, by a search of the workspace and of the scheduler's dispatch of the standard-IO process (scheduler/mod.rs:2576-2581 and its callers), whether anything reaches StandardIoServer::run_available or handle_message (io/standard_io.rs:91-96). If nothing does, THE SYSTEM SHALL remove run_available, handle_message, wait_for_completion and POLL_TIMEOUT with every item only they use, and the handback SHALL quote the search. If something does, wait_for_completion (:216-224) SHALL wait through R1's wait_completions for its own op_id, keeping any other completion it receives for its owner, and POLL_TIMEOUT SHALL be removed.
acceptance: The handback quotes the search and names which branch was taken.
Red, if the path is live (the same file): a standard-IO read's reply arrives with no timeout in the wait, ending on the reply; a completion for another op received while waiting reaches its owner.

boundaries: SHALL NOT change what a process observes: IO results, their order per op and process exits are unchanged.
SHALL NOT add a timer, a background poller, or any wait of a set length, in the code or in the tests; a test's wait ends on an event.
SHALL NOT change the normal workers' park, which is B-181's.
verification: This handwritten brief passes the design gate of this repository, judged by its parsed failures, never by its exit code.

Every gate leg green on the exact final commit (fmt, clippy pedantic -D warnings, the full nextest battery with every feature set the release battery runs, cargo test --doc, the repository's own gates), judged from parsed output, with df and the swap line in START and END, and the venue named; the Linux-only tests of R2 on a Linux venue, or stated NOT CONFIRMED.
Four-heading handback (BLOCKED ON, CHANGED, FOUND, NOT CONFIRMED), with R4's search quoted.
beamr ships it in B-181's release or the next, and liminal and haematite move their beamr pins the same day (Tom's rule 16).
